issues.legal_issue: Business income arising from operations in another contracting state is not taxable in the taxpayer’s state of residence when the treaty allocates fiscal domicile to the state with which the taxpayer has closer personal and economic relations and there is no permanent establishment in the residence state.
material_facts: The taxpayer earned business income from rubber plantations and immovable property located in Malaysia.
The taxpayer had no permanent establishment in India for carrying on the rubber plantation business.
The authorities and the High Court found that the taxpayer’s closer economic relations were with Malaysia.
issues.conclusion: The business income from the Malaysian rubber plantations could not be taxed in India under the treaty.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 90 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a double-taxation agreement prevails over Sections 4 and 5 to the extent its provisions are more beneficial to the taxpayer. Read as a whole, the India–Malaysia agreement determines fiscal domicile by reference to the taxpayer’s personal and economic relations under Article IV and addresses business profits and permanent establishments in Article VII. The Court held that the treaty governed the tax treatment and that the closer economic relations with Malaysia determined the outcome. No earlier cases were relied on in reaching this conclusion.

rule.if: tax_treaty_assessment_appeal and foreign_source_business_income and no_permanent_establishment_in_residence_state and closer_economic_relations_in_source_state

predicates.tax_treaty_assessment_appeal: The dispute arose in an appeal concerning an income-tax assessment governed by an agreement between contracting states.
predicates.foreign_source_business_income: The taxpayer earned business income from operations carried on in a state other than the state of residence.
predicates.no_permanent_establishment_in_residence_: The taxpayer had no permanent establishment in the state of residence for carrying on the business that generated the income.
predicates.closer_economic_relations_in_source_stat: The taxpayer’s economic relations were found to be closer to the state where the income-generating property and business were located.

issues.definition: When an income-tax treaty assessment appeal concerns foreign-source business income, no permanent establishment in the state of residence, and closer economic relations with the source state, the business income is not taxable in the state of residence.

issues.legal_issue: Capital gains arising from the sale of immovable property are income covered by the treaty provision governing income from immovable property.
material_facts: The taxpayer sold immovable property situated in Malaysia and realized short-term capital gains from the sale.
The property was part of the taxpayer’s Malaysian immovable property and plantation interests.
issues.conclusion: The capital gains were income derived from immovable property and were covered by the treaty provision governing income from immovable property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 90 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, makes the applicable agreement prevail over Sections 4 and 5 to the extent the agreement is more beneficial to the taxpayer. The Court treated capital gains as income under the Act, including within the definition of income, and held that the treaty’s Article VI applied to capital gains derived from immovable property. It also relied on Article II’s treatment of taxes of a substantially similar character. The Court did not need to resolve the semantics of “may be taxed.” No earlier cases were relied on in reaching this conclusion.

predicates.tax_treaty_assessment_appeal: The dispute arose in an appeal concerning an income-tax assessment governed by an agreement between contracting states.
predicates.immovable_property_was_sold: The taxpayer transferred immovable property by sale.
predicates.gain_arose_from_sale_of_immovable_proper: The taxpayer realized a capital gain from selling the immovable property.

issues.definition: When an income-tax treaty assessment appeal concerns a sale of immovable property that gives rise to a capital gain, the gain is covered by the treaty article concerning income from immovable property.
